prompt: The edit message rate stays the same, but each document has more collaborators receiving every edit. What changes most directly?

options.text: Outbound fan-out grows even though incoming edit traffic is unchanged
options.explanation: Correct. Each accepted edit must reach more recipients.

options.text: The incoming edit message count necessarily doubles
options.explanation: Wrong. The prompt holds the incoming rate fixed; recipient count changes outgoing work.

options.text: Local echo must wait for every remote recipient
options.explanation: Wrong. Local echo is optimistic and separate from remote delivery and durable acknowledgement.
Wrong. Snapshots help loading and recovery; active collaborators still need updates.

workedExample: Follow one incoming batch. The owner integrates and persists it, then sends it to the other collaborators. Increasing recipients increases network fan-out. Presence and reconnect synchronization add their own traffic, so a fleet-wide edit average is not enough to size hot documents.
